zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّهم إنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكم يَرْجُمُوكُمْ﴾ means: they will kill you by stoning, and "اَلرَّجْمُ" (stoning) is one of the vilest forms of killing. ﴿أوْ يُعِيدُوكم في مِلَّتِهِمْ ولَنْ تُفْلِحُوا إذًا أبَدًا﴾: "إذًا" indicates a condition, that is: "and you will never succeed if you return to their religion."

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أعْثَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ means: We made [people] aware of them. ﴿لِيَعْلَمُوا أنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾, that is: so that those who deny the resurrection may know that Allah's promise is true, and that whoever believes in it may increase in faith. ﴿وَأنَّ السّاعَةَ لا رَيْبَ فِيها إذْ يَتَنازَعُونَ بَيْنَهم أمْرَهُمْ﴾, that is: they were disputing with one another about their affair. It is possible that "إذْ" is in the accusative (manṣūb) through His saying "أعْثَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ", so that the meaning would be: "And thus We made [people] aware of them — that is, acquainted [them] with them — when the dispute about their affair took place." It is also possible that it is in the accusative through His saying ﴿لِيَعْلَمُوا﴾, that is: "so that they might know at the time of their disputing."
His saying: ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا عَلى أمْرِهِمْ لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ مَسْجِدًا﴾: this indicates — and Allah knows best — that when their affair became manifest, those who believed in the resurrection and the raising up [of the dead] prevailed, because mosques belong to the believers.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلاثَةٌ رابِعُهم كَلْبُهُمْ﴾: "ثَلاثَةٌ" is nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject). The meaning is: "Those who dispute about their affair will say: they are three, the fourth of them their dog." ﴿رَجْمًا بِالغَيْبِ﴾, that is: they say that as a "رَجْم", that is, as conjecture and guesswork. Zuhayr said:
؎وَما الحَرْبُ إلّا ما عَلِمْتُمْ وذُقْتُمُ وما هو عَنْها بِالحَدِيثِ المُرَجَّمِ
(War is nothing but what you have known and tasted; and what is said of it is no conjectural tale.)
﴿وَيَقُولُونَ خَمْسَةٌ سادِسُهم كَلْبُهم رَجْمًا بِالغَيْبِ ويَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وثامِنُهم كَلْبُهُمْ﴾: the insertion of the wāw here and its omission from the first are the same [in meaning]. It may also be that the wāw is inserted to indicate the end of the story, and that the matter has been completed.
His saying: ﴿قُلْ رَبِّي أعْلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِمْ ما يَعْلَمُهم إلا قَلِيلٌ﴾: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "The Companions of the Cave were seven, and I am one of the few who know them." The statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, when it is authentically from him, is among the most reliable of exegesis.
His saying: ﴿فَلا تُمارِ فِيهِمْ إلا مِراءً ظاهِرًا﴾ means: do not bring, concerning their affair, anything other than what has been revealed to you; that is, give your ruling on their story according to the manifest [account] that has been sent down to you.
﴿وَلا تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ مِنهُمْ﴾, that is: concerning the Companions of the Cave; ﴿مِنهم أحَدًا﴾, that is: from the People of the Book.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إنِّي فاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا﴾ ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Kahf: 24]: the position of "أنْ" is accusative (naṣb). The meaning is: "Never say 'I will do [it]' except with the will of Allah." So when someone says: "I will do that, if Allah wills (إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ)," it is as though he had said: "I will not do it except by the will of Allah."
His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إذا نَسِيتَ﴾ [al-Kahf: 24], that is: "Whenever you remember that you did not make the exception (istithnāʾ), then make the exception and say: 'if Allah wills.'" ﴿وَقُلْ عَسى أنْ يَهْدِيَنِي رَبِّي لأقْرَبَ مِن هَذا رَشَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 24], that is: say: perhaps He will give me, of signs and proofs of prophethood, what is nearer in right guidance and more indicative than the story of the Companions of the Cave.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَبِثُوا في كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلاثَ مِائَةٍ سِنِينَ وازْدادُوا تِسْعًا﴾: it is permissible for "سِنِينَ" to be accusative (naṣb), and permissible for it to be genitive (jarr). As for the accusative, it is on the meaning: "So they remained in their cave years, three hundred"; and, on another analysis, "سِنِينَ" is conjoined to "ثَلاثَ" as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) and tawkīd (emphasis). It is also permissible for "سِنِينَ" to be a naʿt (adjective) of "المِائَة", while in meaning it refers back to "ثَلاثَ", as the poet said:
؎فِيها اثْنَتانِ وأرْبَعُونَ حَلُوبَةً سُودًا كَخافِيَةِ الغُرابِ الأسْحَمِ
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the jet-black raven.)
He made "سُودًا" a naʿt of "حَلُوبَةً", while in meaning it is a naʿt of the whole number. [Further,] it is possible that "وَلَبِثُوا في كَهْفِهِمْ" is construed with His saying "سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلاثَةٌ رابِعُهم كَلْبُهم", i.e. "and they say: they remained in their cave"; the evidence for this view is His saying: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما لَبِثُوا﴾ [al-Kahf: 26]. And it is possible — and this is the better view in my opinion — that it is a report from Allah: He informed them of the length of their stay and made known that He knows that best; and it is more eloquent as a sign concerning them that the truth is that they did remain this entire number.
As for His saying: ﴿وازْدادُوا تِسْعًا﴾, it does not mean "and they added nine nights" nor "nine hours", because a number is known by its specification (tafsīr), and when its specification has preceded, what has preceded makes it unnecessary to mention the specification again. You say: "عِنْدِي مِائَةٌ دِرْهَمٍ وخَمْسَةٌ" (I have a hundred dirhams and five), and the mention of the dirham indicates [what] the five [are]. [Translator's note: the text as printed reads "مِائَةٌ دِرْهَمٍ"; the usual construct form is "مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ".]
Likewise His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكم ويَذَرُونَ أزْواجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأنْفُسِهِنَّ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ وعَشْرًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 234]. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: "وَعَشْرًا" means "and ten periods", and each of those periods is a day and a night. The Arabs say: "ما رَأيْتُهُ مُنْذُ عَشْرٍ" (I have not seen him for ten) and "أتَيْتُهُ لِعَشْرٍ خَلَوْنَ" (I came to him when ten had passed), and they give the nights precedence over mentioning the days, the days being included in the nights; and the nights together with the day form a known period of time. So the feminine form of "عَشْر" indicates that "months" are not meant by it. This is the best that has been said in explaining this verse.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أبْصِرْ بِهِ وأسْمِعْ﴾: the scholars agree that its meaning is: "How well He hears and how well He sees!" That is: He knows the story of the Companions of the Cave and others.
His saying: ﴿وَلا يُشْرِكُ في حُكْمِهِ أحَدًا﴾ was also read "وَلا تُشْرِكْ" as a prohibition. The verse — and Allah knows best — indicates one of two meanings. The first is that He made mention of His knowledge and His power, and then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He does not make anyone a partner in His judgement concerning what He reports of the unseen, as He said: ﴿عالِمُ الغَيْبِ فَلا يُظْهِرُ عَلى غَيْبِهِ أحَدًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 26]. Likewise when it is read "وَلا تُشْرِكْ — with the tāʾ — في حُكْمِهِ أحَدًا", that is: do not ascribe knowledge of the unseen to anyone. And it may be — and Allah knows best, and this is a good, far-reaching [meaning] — in the sense that it is not permissible for any judge to judge except by what Allah has judged, or by what the judgement of Allah indicates; no one may judge of his own accord and so become a partner of Allah in His judgement, commanding a ruling as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَدًا﴾ means: you will not find any turning away from His command and His prohibition, nor any refuge except in Him. Likewise: ﴿لا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِماتِهِ﴾, that is: whatever Allah has reported and whatever He has commanded, there is none who can change it.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿واصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهم بِالغَداةِ والعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وجْهَهُ﴾ was also read "بِالغُدْوَةِ والعَشِيِّ". "بِالغَداةِ والعَشِيِّ" is better according to all the scholars, because "غُدْوَةٌ" is a definite noun that does not take the alif and lām [the definite article], and those who added the alif and lām treated it as indefinite. The meaning of "يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهم بِالغَداةِ والعَشِيِّ" is: they call upon Him with [the affirmation of His] oneness and with sincerity towards Him, and they worship Him. ﴿يُرِيدُونَ وجْهَهُ﴾, that is: "they intend none but Him by their worship."
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَعْدُ عَيْناكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ means: "Do not turn your gaze to others than them among people of rank and adornment." It is related «that a group of the great men of the idolaters said to the Prophet — upon him be peace —: "Send away from you these people whose smell is like the smell of sheep; they are clients (mawālī) and not nobles — so that we may sit with you and learn from you," meaning Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Bilāl and those like them. So Allah commanded him not to do that, and to give his attention to the believers and not to turn to others than them, and He said: ﴿وَلا تَعْدُ عَيْناكَ عَنْهم تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا ولا تُطِعْ مَن أغْفَلْنا قَلْبَهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِنا واتَّبَعَ هَواهُ وكانَ أمْرُهُ فُرُطًا﴾», that is: his affair was negligence (التَّفْرِيط), and "اَلتَّفْرِيطُ" is putting incapacity first.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقُلِ الحَقُّ مِن رَبِّكم فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾: the meaning is: "And say: what I have brought you is the truth from your Lord." ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾: this speech is not a command to them such that whichever of it they do they would be obedient in it; rather it is speech of threat and warning. He has made clear after it what each party, believer and unbeliever, will have. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنّا أعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ نارًا﴾. The meaning of "أعْتَدْنا" is: We have made it a provision (عِتاد) for them, as you say: "I have made this a preparation (عُدَّة) for that." "اَلْعِتادُ" is the thing that is fixed and lasting.
His saying: ﴿أحاطَ بِهِمْ سُرادِقُها﴾ means: a pavilion (سُرادِق) of punishment came to be over them. "اَلسُّرادِقُ" is anything that surrounds a thing, such as "اَلشَّقَّةُ" (the canvas strip) of a tent, and "اَلْحائِطُ" (the wall) that encloses a thing.
His saying: ﴿كالمُهْلِ﴾ means that they will be relieved with water like molten lead (الرَّصاص), that is, brass and silver; everything of these things that you melt is "مُهْلٌ". It is also said: "اَلْمُهْلُ" is the dregs of oil; and it is also said: "اَلْمُهْلُ" is the pus of a wound. ﴿يَشْوِي الوُجُوهَ﴾, that is: when it is brought near to be drunk, it scorches the face with its heat. ﴿بِئْسَ الشَّرابُ وساءَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا﴾: "مُرْتَفَقًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). "مُرْتَفَقًا" means a dwelling place; and the lexicographers said: "مُرْتَفَقًا" means a place of reclining, and they recited:
؎إنِّي أرِقْتُ فَبِتُّ اللَّيْلَ مُرْتَفِقًا كَأنَّ عَيْنِيَ فِيها الصّابُ مَذْبُوحُ
(I lay sleepless and spent the night leaning on my elbow, as though my eye had bitter aloe-sap squeezed into it.)

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلا﴾: the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" here is on three possible analyses. The first is that it is on the implication of "إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلًا مِنهُمْ" (We do not let the reward of whoever of them does good work be lost); there was no need to mention "مِنهُمْ" because Allah the Exalted has informed us that He nullifies the works of those other than the believers. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ مِنهم مَغْفِرَةً وأجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 29]. And it is possible that the khabar of "إنَّ" is:
[Translator's note: the source text of this entry breaks off here; the remaining analyses are not present in the entry as provided.]

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ [is the khabar (predicate)], and His saying ﴿إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 30] has been used to separate the noun [of إنَّ] from its khabar, because it contains a mention of what is in the first, since "مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلًا" stands in the place of "اَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا". A third analysis is that the khabar is "إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن أحْسَنَ عَمَلًا" in the sense of "إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَهُمْ" (We do not let their reward be lost), because the mention of "مَن" is like the mention of "اَلَّذِي", and the mention of doing good work is like the mention of faith. So it would be like your saying: "إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصّالِحاتِ إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أجْرَ مَن آمَنَ" (Those who do righteous deeds — Allah does not let the reward of whoever believes be lost), which is like your saying: "إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أجْرَهُمْ" (Allah does not let their reward be lost). ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: the meaning of "جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ" is: gardens of permanent residence.
It was said in exegesis: "جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ" are gardens among the four gardens that Allah has prepared for His friends. ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ﴾: "أساوِرَ" is the plural of "أسْوِرَةٌ", and "أسْوِرَةٌ" is the plural of "سِوارٌ" (bracelet). One says: "هُوَ سِوارٌ في اليَدِ" (it is a bracelet on the hand), with kasra; "سَوارٌ" has also been reported, and Quṭrub reported "إسْوارٌ", and he mentioned that "أساوِرَ" is the plural of "إسْوارٌ" with the yāʾ dropped, because the plural of "إسْوارٌ" is "أساوِيرُ".
﴿وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيابًا خُضْرًا مِن سُنْدُسٍ وإسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾: "اَلسُّنْدُسُ" and "اَلْإسْتَبْرَقُ" are two kinds of silk. ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها عَلى الأرائِكِ نِعْمَ الثَّوابُ وحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا﴾: the singular of "اَلْأرائِكُ" is "أرِيكَةٌ", and "اَلْأرائِكُ" are the couches inside curtained canopies (الحِجال). "مُرْتَفَقًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and we have already explained "اَلْمُرْتَفَقُ".

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿واضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلا رَجُلَيْنِ﴾: the idolaters had asked the Prophet ﷺ — on the advice of the Jews to them that they should ask the Prophet ﷺ — about the story of the Companions of the Cave, about the spirit, and about these two men. So Allah made the answer known to him, and that it is a parable for him — upon him be peace — and for the unbelievers, and a parable for all who believe in Allah and all who stubbornly turn from Him and disbelieve in Him. So He the Exalted said: ﴿واضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلا رَجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنا لأحَدِهِما جَنَّتَيْنِ مِن أعْنابٍ وحَفَفْناهُما بِنَخْلٍ﴾. "رَجُلَيْنِ" is accusative in the sense of the object, with the meaning: "And strike for them a parable: the parable of two men." "وَحَفَفْناهُما بِنَخْلٍ", that is: "We made the palm trees surround them both." One says: "قَدْ حَفَّ القَوْمُ بِزَيْدٍ" (the people surrounded Zayd) when they are encircling him. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُما زَرْعًا﴾

zajjaj:33-33.t: So Allah made known that their cultivation was complete and continuous, with nothing separating them except cultivation, and He informed us that they were both complete in yielding their produce from their palms, their vines and the crops between them. He said: ﴿كِلْتا الجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَها ولَمْ تَظْلِمْ مِنهُ شَيْئًا﴾, that is: it did not diminish any of it. He said "آتَتْ" and did not say "آتَتا", referring it back to "كِلْتا", because the form of "كِلْتا" is the form of a singular, and the meaning is: "Each one of them gave its produce." Had it been "آتَتا", it would have been permissible, with the meaning: "The two gardens, both of them gave their produce." ﴿وَفَجَّرْنا خِلالَهُما نَهَرًا﴾: had it been read "نَهْرًا", it would have been permissible; one says "نَهَرٌ" and "نَهْرٌ". So He informed us that their watering was from the water of a river, which is among the most abundant of waterings.

zajjaj:34-34.t:
﴿وَكانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ﴾ was also read "ثُمُرٌ". It was said: "اَلثَّمَرُ" is what the trees put forth, and "اَلثُّمُرُ" is wealth; one says: "قَدْ ثَمَّرَ فُلانٌ مالًا" (so-and-so has grown wealth). "اَلثَّمَرُ" is better here, because His saying ﴿كِلْتا الجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَها﴾ [al-Kahf: 33] has already indicated the fruit. It is also permissible that "ثَمَرٌ" be the plural of "ثَمَرَةٌ", [as are] "ثِمارٌ" and "ثُمُرٌ".
His saying: ﴿فَقالَ لِصاحِبِهِ وهو يُحاوِرُهُ أنا أكْثَرُ مِنكَ مالا وأعَزُّ نَفَرًا﴾: "مالًا" and "نَفَرًا" are both accusative as tamyīz (specification). He told him that he was mightier than him in supporters, that is, he was informing him that his helpers were many.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ وهو ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾: everyone who disbelieves in Allah wrongs his own soul, because he makes it enter the Fire, which holds everlasting punishment; so what wrong to the soul is greater than this?!
His saying: ﴿ما أظُنُّ أنْ تَبِيدَ هَذِهِ أبَدًا﴾ ﴿وَما أظُنُّ السّاعَةَ قائِمَةً﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]: so he declared his disbelief in the Hour and his disbelief in the passing away of this world. ﴿وَلَئِنْ رُدِدْتُ إلى رَبِّي لأجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِنها مُنْقَلَبًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]: this indicates that his believing companion had informed him that the Hour will come and that he will be raised, so he answered him by saying: "And if I am returned to my Lord, as you have told me that I will be raised, He will certainly give me in the Hereafter better than what He gave me in this world, because He did not give me this in this world except that He will give me more if the matter in the Hereafter is like this." So his companion said to him, rejecting this statement of his: ﴿أكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوّاكَ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 37], that is: then He completed you — yet you denied the matter of the resurrection, to the point that you doubted it. We have been informed that one who doubts the command of Allah is an unbeliever, and that some suspicion is a sin, that is, falsehood; and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿وَما خَلَقْنا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما باطِلا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 27]

zajjaj:38-38.t:
Then his companion informed him that he affirmed the oneness of Allah, and that whatever possession and blessing a person is able to attain, he has no strength and no power over it except through Allah. He said: ﴿لَكِنّا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي ولا أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّي أحَدًا﴾, and his address indicates that the owner of the two gardens was an idolater (mushrik), worshipping others along with Allah.
In His saying ﴿لَكِنّا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي﴾ there are five possibilities: "لَكِنَّ هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي", with the nūn doubled and with fatḥa, pausing on it with the alif and joining it [to what follows] without the alif; it is also read "لَكِنّا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي" with the alif in continuous speech; and it is read "لَكِنْ هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي" with the nūn quiescent; and it is permissible — though I know of no one who read it so — "لَكِنَنَ هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي", with two nūns both carrying fatḥa.
And "لَكِنَنا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي", with two nūns and an alif, is permissible. As for whoever reads with the doubled nūn, the meaning is: "لَكِنَّ أنا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي" (But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord); the hamza was thrown onto the nūn, which then took a fatḥa, and two letters of the same kind came together, so the first nūn was assimilated into the second; and the alif was dropped in continuous speech, because it is retained in pause and dropped in continuous speech. Whoever reads "لَكِنّا" and retains the alif in continuous speech, just as it is retained in pause, follows the dialect of those who say "أنا قُمْتُ" (I stood) retaining the alif. The poet said:
؎أنا سَيْفُ العَشِيرَةِ فاعْرِفُونِي حَمِيدًا قَدْ تَذَرَّيْتُ السَّناما
(I am the sword of the clan, so know me as Ḥumayd; I have mounted the very top of the hump [i.e. attained the summit of honour].)
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The retention of the alif of "أنا" in continuous speech in all this is anomalous (shādhdh); but whoever retains it does so on the basis of the pause, just as the hāʾ is retained in His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 10] and ﴿كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19]. Whoever reads "لَكِنَّ هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي" — it is "لَكِنَّ" alone, with no noun with it. Whoever reads "لَكِنَنَ" does not assimilate, because the two nūns belong to two words; and likewise whoever says "لَكِنَنا" with two nūns and an alif, on the analogy of "لَكِنَّ أنا", does not assimilate, because the two nūns belong to two words.
There are three dialectal forms (lughāt) for "أنا" in continuous speech. The best of them is "أنا قُمْتُ", like His saying ﴿أنا رَبُّكُمُ﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 24], without the alif in pronunciation; "أنا قُمْتُ" with the alif retained is permissible, but very weak; and they reported "أنْ قُمْتُ" with the nūn quiescent, which is also weak. As for "لَكِنّا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي", it is the good [reading], with the alif retained, because the hamza has been dropped from "أنا", so retaining the alif became a compensation for the hamza. This is everything that this word can bear.
The good and eloquent form is what is in the codex (muṣḥaf) of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, which we did not mention among these readings because it differs from the [ʿUthmānic] codex, namely "لَكِنَّ أنا هو اللَّهُ رَبِّي"; this is the original form. Everything that has been read is good and eloquent, and I do not reject reading with this, because omission occurs frequently in the Book with yāʾs and hamzas, and it is read both with the omission and in full, as in His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 6] — whoever reads "اَلدّاعِي" is correct, and whoever reads "اَلدّاعِ" is correct. Likewise whoever reads "لَكِنّا" or "لَكِنَّ أنا" is correct. But the best course is to follow the Readers and to keep to what is transmitted, for reading is a sunna (an established practice). The more a word is transmitted and the more it is read, the more it is the one to be followed. Whatever is permissible in Arabic but no reader has read with it — do not read with it, for reading with it is an innovation (bidʿa). And everything that is rarely transmitted and is weak in the view of the scholars of Arabic falls within the anomalous (shudhūdh), and one should not read with it.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا إذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ﴾: "اَلْجَنَّةُ" is the orchard. The meaning of "وَلَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not), and the import of the speech is rebuke. ﴿قُلْتَ ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: "ما" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is: "You said: the matter is what Allah wills." It is also possible that "ما" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), in the sense of a condition and its consequence (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ), with the apodosis (jawāb) implied; the interpretation would then be: "Whatever Allah wills, comes to be." The apodosis is implied just as the apodosis of "لَوْ" is implied in His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الجِبالُ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 31], the meaning being: "it would have been this Qur'an."
His saying: ﴿لا قُوَّةَ إلا بِاللَّهِ﴾: the preferred [reading] is the accusative without tanwīn, as a negation [with the lā of generic negation], as He said: "لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ". "لا قُوَّةٌ إلّا بِاللَّهِ" is also permissible, in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with "بِاللَّهِ" as the khabar (predicate). The meaning is that no one is strong in his habitual conduct, nor in what his right hand possesses, except through Allah, and he has nothing except what Allah wills.
His saying: ﴿إنْ تَرَنِ أنا أقَلَّ مِنكَ﴾: "أقَلَّ" is accusative, being the second object of "تَرَنِي". "أنا" is fit for two things: if you wish, it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the nūn and the yāʾ; and if you wish, it is a separating pronoun (faṣl), as you say: "كُنْتَ أنْتَ القائِمَ يا هَذا" (You were the one standing, O you). The nominative "أقَلُّ" is also permissible, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it so: "إنْ تَرَنِ أنا أقَلُّ مِنكَ مالًا", with "أنا" as a mubtadaʾ and "أقَلُّ" as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause in the position of the second object of "تَرَنِي".

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿فَعَسى رَبِّي أنْ يُؤْتِيَنِي خَيْرًا مِن جَنَّتِكَ﴾: it is possible that he meant "in this world" or "in the Hereafter". "وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْها حُسْبانًا مِّنَ السَّماءِ": this is a subtle place that needs to be explained. "اَلْحُسْبانُ" in the language is the reckoning (الحِساب); He the Exalted said: ﴿الشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 5], meaning "by reckoning". So the meaning in this verse is: "that He send upon it the punishment of a reckoning", and that reckoning is the reckoning of what your hands have earned.
His saying: ﴿فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا﴾: "اَلصَّعِيدُ" is the path in which there is no vegetation, and likewise "اَلزَّلَقُ".

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿أوْ يُصْبِحَ ماؤُها غَوْرًا﴾ means "غائِرًا" (sunk into the earth). One says: "ماءٌ غَوْرٌ" (sunken water) and "مِياهٌ غَوْرٌ" (sunken waters); "غَوْرٌ" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like "عَدْلٌ" and "رِضًى".
His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا﴾ means: "It sinks, so that you are unable to find any trace that you could seek it by."

zajjaj:42-42.t:
﴿وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ﴾, that is: "Allah made the punishment encompass his fruit." ﴿فَأصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلى ما أنْفَقَ فِيها﴾
Turning over the palms is something people often do [in regret]. ﴿وَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها﴾, that is: its walls are standing with no roofs upon them; its roofs have collapsed and come to lie on its floor. "اَلْعُرُوشُ" are the roofs, so the walls became as though they were upon the roofs.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ فِئَةٌ يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: "يَنْصُرُونَهُ" is construed according to the meaning of "فِئَةٌ" (a band); the meaning is: "and he had no people to help him." Had it been "تَنْصُرُهُ", it would have been permissible, as He said: ﴿فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 13].
﴿وَما كانَ مُنْتَصِرًا﴾: nor was he himself able to help himself.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿هُنالِكَ الوَلايَةُ لِلَّهِ الحَقِّ﴾ is also read "اَلْوِلايَةُ — with kasra and with fatḥa on the wāw — لِلَّهِ الحَقِّ", and it is also read "اَلْحَقُّ". The meaning is: "In such a situation the walāya (protecting friendship) of Allah becomes clear," that is: "at that time His help becomes clear — the friend of Allah is the one whom Allah takes under His protection." Whoever reads "اَلْحَقُّ" in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of "الوَلايَة"; and whoever reads "اَلْحَقِّ" in the genitive makes it a naʿt of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. "اَلْحَقَّ" [in the accusative] is also permissible, though I know of no one who read it so; its accusative would be as a maṣdar (verbal noun) for emphasis, as you say: "هُنالِكَ الحَقَّ", that is: "أحُقُّ الحَقَّ" (I affirm the truth truly).
His saying: ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوابًا وخَيْرٌ عُقْبًا﴾ [is also read] "عُقُبًا", and "وخَيْرٌ عُقْبى", on the pattern of "بُشْرى", is also permissible. "ثَوابًا" and "عُقْبًا" are both accusative as tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿واضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا كَماءٍ أنْـزَلْناهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ فاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَباتُ الأرْضِ﴾: its interpretation is that [the water] penetrated the plants until it mingled with them, and the plants took on their adornment. ﴿فَأصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا﴾: "اَلْهَشِيمُ" is the dry vegetation that the wind blows about. ﴿تَذْرُوهُ الرِّياحُ﴾ is also read "اَلرِّيحُ". In "تَذْرُوهُ" there are two dialectal forms with which it is not read: "تُذْرِيهِ", with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, and "تَذْرِيهِ", with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the life of this world passes away; the proof of this is that what has passed of it is as though it had never been. And He made known that its likeness is this likeness.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِرًا﴾, that is: able to bring into being and to bring to an end.
If someone asks: the speech is "كانَ اللَّهُ" (Allah was) — [what does it mean?], its interpretation is that the power of His that you have witnessed is not something new with Him, and that He was thus and has never ceased to be so. This is the view of Sībawayh. Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِرًا﴾ means: He was able over it before it came to be. Some said: "كانَ" from Allah stands in the place of "كائِنٌ" (being) and "يَكُونُ" (is/will be). Al-Ḥasan's statement on this is good and fine.
The view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl is the view of the skilled grammarians, as we have described, because they say: the Arabs were addressed only in their own language, and the Qur'an was revealed in what they understand and use in addressing one another; and the Arabs do not know "كانَ" in the sense of "يَكُونُ" unless some particle enters upon the word that shifts it to the sense of the future; likewise they do not know the past in the sense of the present. This is the explanation of what is in the Qur'an of this kind, such as His saying: "وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا", "وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا"; and we have explained it before this place.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿والباقِياتُ الصّالِحاتُ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَوابًا وخَيْرٌ أمَلا﴾: "اَلْباقِياتُ الصّالِحاتُ" (the enduring good deeds) are the five prayers; it was also said that they are "سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ، والحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، ولا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ واللَّهُ أكْبَرُ" (Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest). And "اَلْباقِياتُ الصّالِحاتُ" — and Allah knows best — are "every righteous deed whose reward endures". So the five prayers, affirming the oneness of Allah and glorifying Him are included in the enduring good deeds, and likewise alms, fasting, jihād and all deeds of goodness and piety.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الجِبالَ وتَرى الأرْضَ بارِزَةً﴾: "يَوْمَ" is accusative in the sense of recitation and remembrance; the meaning is: "And remember the day when We set the mountains in motion." It is also possible that its accusative is on [the construction] "والباقِياتُ الصّالِحاتُ خَيْرٌ يَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الجِبالَ" (the enduring good deeds are better on the day We set the mountains in motion), that is: "better on the Day of Resurrection than the deeds whose sins remain."
His saying: ﴿وَتَرى الأرْضَ بارِزَةً﴾ means: "laid bare", its mountains having been set in motion, its trees uprooted and its buildings gone, so that it remains laid bare, having cast out what was in it and become empty.
His saying: ﴿وَحَشَرْناهم فَلَمْ نُغادِرْ مِنهم أحَدًا﴾, that is: "We did not leave any one of them behind."

zajjaj:48-48.t:
﴿وَعُرِضُوا عَلى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا﴾: its meaning is that all of them are visible to Allah; their whole company is seen just as each one of them is seen, no one screening another.
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا كَما خَلَقْناكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾, that is: We have raised you as We created you. It has come in exegesis that they will be gathered naked, uncircumcised (غُرْلًا) and barefoot. "غُرْلًا" is the plural of "أغْرَلُ", which is the uncircumcised one (الأقْلَف).
His saying: ﴿بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ ألَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكم مَوْعِدًا﴾, that is: rather you claimed that you would not be raised, because Allah — exalted be His praise — had promised them the resurrection.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَوُضِعَ الكِتابُ﴾ means — and Allah knows best —: "The book of every person was placed in his right hand or his left hand." ﴿فَتَرى المُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمّا فِيهِ ويَقُولُونَ يا ويْلَتَنا﴾: everyone who falls into ruin cries out "woe!". ﴿مالِ هَذا الكِتابِ لا يُغادِرُ صَغِيرَةً ولا كَبِيرَةً إلا أحْصاها﴾, that is: "not leaving out any small [deed]". ﴿وَوَجَدُوا ما عَمِلُوا حاضِرًا ولا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أحَدًا﴾, that is: He only punishes them, putting the punishment in its proper place in requiting sins. The lexicographers agree that ẓulm (wrongdoing) is putting a thing in other than its proper place.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إلا إبْلِيسَ كانَ مِنَ الجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾: His saying ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ is evidence that he was commanded to prostrate along with the angels. Most of what is in exegesis is that Iblīs was not one of the angels, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned that he was of the jinn, standing [among them] in the position of Adam among humankind. It has also been said that the jinn are a kind of angel who were the keepers of the earth; and it was said: the keepers of the gardens.
If someone asks: how was he excepted along with the mention of the angels, when He said ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إلا إبْلِيسَ﴾ — how did the exception (istithnāʾ) occur when he is not of the first [group]? The answer to this is that he was commanded together with them to prostrate, so he was excepted in that he did not prostrate. The evidence for this is that you say: "أمَرْتُ عَبْدِي وإخْوَتِي، فَأطاعُونِي إلّا عَبْدِي" (I commanded my slave and my brothers, and they obeyed me except my slave). Likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77] — and the Lord of the worlds, there is nothing like Him, yet His mention has occurred in the exception, and it is an exception not from the first [group]; and no one can understand the meaning of the speech other than this. ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ has three possible interpretations. Its meaning may be: "he went out from his Lord's command"; one says: "فَسَقَتِ الرُّطَبَةُ" (the fresh date came out) when it comes out of its skin. Quṭrub said: its meaning may be: "he transgressed by rejecting his Lord's command." The view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl — and it is the truth in our view — is that the meaning of "فَسَقَ عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّهِ" is: transgression came upon him when he was commanded, so he disobeyed, and the cause of his transgression was his Lord's command; as you say: "أطْعَمَهُ عَنْ جُوعٍ، وكَساهُ عَنْ عُرْيٍ" (he fed him because of hunger and clothed him because of nakedness). The meaning is: "the cause of his transgression was the command to prostrate", just as the cause of feeding was hunger and the cause of clothing was nakedness.
His saying: ﴿بِئْسَ لِلظّالِمِينَ بَدَلا﴾ means: wretched is what the wrongdoers took in exchange for the Lord of Might, Majestic and Mighty — [namely] Iblīs.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿ما أشْهَدْتُهم خَلْقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ ولا خَلْقَ أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, that is: they did not exist when I created the heavens and the earth. ﴿وَما كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ المُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا﴾ is also read "وَما كُنْتَ مُتَّخِذَ المُضِلِّينَ", with fatḥa on the tāʾ. The meaning with the fatḥa is: "It is not for you, O Muḥammad, to take those who lead astray as helpers." The ḍamma on the tāʾ is the [established] reading, and on it the meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is telling of His power, and that He does not seek support (yaʿtaḍidu) in it, nor in His help, from those who lead astray. "اَلِاعْتِضادُ" is seeking strength and asking for assistance; one says: "اِعْتَضَدْتُ بِفُلانٍ", meaning: I sought help from him. "عَضُدًا" has five forms, two of which are common and good: "عَضُدًا", with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the ḍād, and "عُضُدًا", with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the ḍād. "عَضْدًا" and "عُضْدًا", with the ḍād quiescent and ḍamma or fatḥa on the ʿayn, are also permissible. "عَضِدًا", with kasra on the ḍād, has been transmitted, and in "عَضِدًا" with kasra on the ḍād, "عَضْدًا" is permissible.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نادُوا شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ﴾: He attributed them to Himself according to their [own] claim.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم مَوْبِقًا﴾: We placed between them, of punishment, that which destroys them (يُوبِقُهُمْ), that is, ruins them. "اَلْمَوْبِقُ" is the place of destruction. One says: "وَبِقَ الرَّجُلُ يَوْبَقُ وبَقًا" (the man perished), and one also says "يَيْبَقُ", and "بائِقٌ". There is another dialectal form in it: "وَبَقَ يَبِقُ وبُوقًا", and "هُوَ وابِقٌ"; for the first, it is "وَبِقٌ".

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَرَأى المُجْرِمُونَ النّارَ﴾: the reading is "وَرَأى", and "وَراءَ المُجْرِمُونَ" is permissible, like "وَراعَ" [i.e. with metathesis], as Kuthayyir said:
؎وَكُلُّ خَلِيلٍ راءَنِي فَهْوَ قائِلٌ مِنَ اجْلِكَ هَذا هامَةُ اليَوْمِ أوْ غَدِ
(Every friend who sees me says: because of you, this man will be a corpse today or tomorrow.)
His saying: ﴿فَظَنُّوا أنَّهم مُواقِعُوها﴾ means: "they were certain", and we have explained this. ﴿وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْها مَصْرِفًا﴾, that is: a way of turning aside. Abū Kabīr said:
؎أزُهَيْرُ هَلْ عَنْ شَيْبَةٍ مِن مَصْرِفٍ ∗∗∗ أمْ لا خُلُودَ لِباذِلٍ مُتَكَلِّفِ
(O Zuhayr, is there any turning away from grey hair, or is there no immortality for one who gives generously and strains himself?)

zajjaj:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا في هَذا القُرْآنِ لِلنّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ﴾, that is: of every example that they need; that is, We have made it clear to them.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ الإنْسانُ أكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلا﴾ means: the unbeliever was; and what indicates this is His saying: ﴿وَيُجادِلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الحَقَّ﴾ [al-Kahf: 56].
If someone asks: does anyone other than the human being dispute? The answer to that is that Iblīs disputed, and every rational being among the angels and the jinn disputes, but the human being is the most disputatious of these things.

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَما مَنَعَ النّاسَ أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إذْ جاءَهُمُ الهُدى﴾: the position of "أنْ" is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "And nothing prevented people from faith." ﴿إلا أنْ تَأْتِيَهم سُنَّةُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "except seeking that the way of the ancients should come upon them." "The way of the ancients" (سُنَّةُ الأوَّلِينَ) is that they saw the punishment with their own eyes; so the idolaters sought it when they said: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ أوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ العَذابُ قُبُلا﴾ is also read "قِبَلًا", with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ; "قُبْلًا", with the bāʾ quiescent, is permissible, but no one has read it so. The position of "أنْ" in His saying "إلّا أنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ" is nominative (rafʿ). The interpretation of "قِبَلًا" is: face to face; and the interpretation of "قُبُلًا" is: the plural of "قَبِيلٌ" (kind), the meaning being: "or the punishment should come upon them in various kinds." It is also possible that the interpretation of "قُبُلًا" is in the sense of "from the front" (مِن قُبُلٍ), that is, from what faces them.

zajjaj:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَدْعُهم إلى الهُدى فَلَنْ يَهْتَدُوا إذًا أبَدًا﴾: these are people of whom Allah has reported that they are among those [whose hearts are] sealed. He said: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ أكِنَّةً أنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾. "أكِنَّةٌ" is the plural of "كِنانَةٌ", which is a covering, like "عِنانٌ" and "أعِنَّةٌ". [Translator's note: the text reads "كِنانَةٌ"; the singular normally given for "أكِنَّة" is "كِنان", which also matches the cited parallel "عِنان / أعِنَّة".] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that these very people will never be guided.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿لَنْ يَجِدُوا مِن دُونِهِ مَوْئِلا﴾: "اَلْمَوْئِلُ" is a place of escape. One says: "وَألَ يَئِلُ" when someone escapes.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ القُرى أهْلَكْناهم لَمّا ظَلَمُوا﴾: the meaning is: "And the people of those towns, We destroyed them." By it are meant those nations of the past that He destroyed, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Lot, and those mentioned as destroyed.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ مَوْعِدًا﴾, that is: an appointed term. There are three forms in it: "لِمُهْلَكِهِمْ" — and the interpretation of "اَلْمُهْلَكُ" is of two kinds: as a maṣdar (verbal noun) and as [a noun of] time. The maṣdar sense is: "for their destruction", and the time sense is: "for the time of their destruction". Every past verb on the pattern "أفْعَلَ" has its maṣdar as "مُفْعَلٌ" or "إفْعالٌ", and its noun of time is "مُفْعَلٌ", and likewise its noun of place. You say: "أدْخَلْتُهُ مُدْخَلًا" (I brought him in a bringing-in), and "هَذا مُدْخَلُهُ", that is: the place through which Zayd enters; and "هَذا مُدْخَلُهُ", that is: the time of his being brought in.
It is also permissible to read "لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ", taking "مَهْلِكٌ" as a noun of time from "هَلَكَ يَهْلِكُ"; [one says] "هَذا زَمَنُ مَهْلِكِهِ" (this is the time of his perishing), like "جَلَسَ يَجْلِسُ" when you mean the place or the time. If you mean the maṣdar, you say "مَهْلَكٌ", with fatḥa on the lām, like "مَجْلَسٌ". One says: "أتَتِ النّاقَةُ عَلى مَضْرَبِها", that is: at the time of her being covered [by the stallion]. And you say: "جَلَسَ مَجْلَسًا", with fatḥa on the lām, and likewise "هَلَكَ مَهْلَكًا", that is: "هُلْكًا" (a perishing). The position of "تِلْكَ القُرى" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); "اَلْقُرى" is a clarifying adjective (ṣifa) of it, and "أهْلَكْناهُمْ" is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. It is also permissible for the position of "تِلْكَ القُرى" to be accusative, with "أهْلَكْناهُمْ" explaining the [omitted] governing verb, so that the meaning is: "And We destroyed those towns — We destroyed them."

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ مُوسى لِفَتاهُ﴾: if you wish, you may say it with imāla (inclination of the vowel) and kasra, which is the dialect of Tamīm, while the people of the Ḥijāz pronounce it with fatḥa and full [open] articulation. It is related in exegesis that his young man was Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn. ﴿لا أبْرَحُ حَتّى أبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ البَحْرَيْنِ﴾: the meaning of "لا أبْرَحُ" is "لا أزالُ" (I will not cease). Had it been "لا أزُولُ" (I will not move away), it would have been absurd, because if he did not move from his place he would not cross any land. "لا أبْرَحُ" in the sense of "لا أزالُ" is found in the speech of the Arabs; the poet said:
؎وَأبْرَحُ ما أدامَ اللَّهُ قَوْمِي عَلى الأعْداءِ مُنْتَطِقًا مُجِيدا
(And I shall not cease, as long as Allah preserves my people, to be girded [for battle] against the enemies, riding a fine steed.)
That is: I shall not cease.
He called him his young man (فَتاهُ) only because he used to serve him; the evidence for that is Moses's saying: ﴿آتِنا غَداءَنا﴾ [al-Kahf: 62].
His saying: ﴿حُقُبًا﴾: "اَلْحُقُبُ" is eighty years. The meeting place of the two seas was the place where Moses was promised to meet al-Khaḍir — upon him be peace. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wished to let Moses know — even though he had been given the Torah — that someone else had also been given knowledge that he did not have; so he was promised a meeting with al-Khaḍir.

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿فَلَمّا بَلَغا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِما﴾: by this are meant Moses and Yūshaʿ. ﴿نَسِيا حُوتَهُما﴾: it was — according to what is related — a salted fish, and it was a sign for Moses at the place where he would meet al-Khaḍir. ﴿فاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ في البَحْرِ سَرَبًا﴾: Allah brought the fish to life so that it slipped away into the sea. "سَرَبًا" is accusative in two ways. [First,] as an object, as when you say: "اِتَّخَذْتُ طَرِيقِي في السَّرَبِ" (I took my way through the tunnel) and "اِتَّخَذْتُ طَرِيقِي مَكانَ كَذا وكَذا" (I took my way such-and-such a place); it would then be a second object, as when you say: "اِتَّخَذْتُ زَيْدًا وكِيلًا" (I took Zayd as an agent). [Second,] it is possible for "سَرَبًا" to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by "فاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ في البَحْرِ"; the meaning would then be: "They forgot their fish, and the fish made its way in the sea", then He explained how that was, as though He had said: "the fish slipped away a slipping away (سَرَبَ الحُوتُ سَرَبًا)." The meaning of "نَسِيا حُوتَهُما" is that the forgetting on Yūshaʿ's part was [forgetting] to bring it forward, and the forgetting on Moses's part was [forgetting] to give him some instruction about it.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ أرَأيْتَ إذْ أوَيْنا إلى الصَّخْرَةِ﴾: the rock was the place of the appointment.
﴿فَإنِّي نَسِيتُ الحُوتَ﴾: this is the saying of Yūshaʿ to Moses when Moses said: "آتِنا غَداءَنا" (bring us our morning meal), and the fish was part of the provisions for their meal. He said: ﴿وَما أنْسانِيهُ إلا الشَّيْطانُ أنْ أذْكُرَهُ﴾ — kasra and ḍamma on the hāʾ are both permissible in "أنْسانِيهُ". ﴿أنْ أذْكُرَهُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ, because the remembering encompasses the hāʾ in meaning [i.e. a badal of inclusion]; the meaning is: "And none made me forget to mention it except Satan." ﴿واتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ في البَحْرِ عَجَبًا﴾: "عَجَبًا" is accusative in two ways: [first,] as part of Yūshaʿ's saying: "and the fish took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner"; and it is possible that Yūshaʿ said: "the fish took its way into the sea", and Moses answered him saying: "عَجَبًا" (how wondrous!), as though he said: "I marvel a marvelling."

zajjaj:64-64.t: Then he said: ﴿ذَلِكَ ما كُنّا نَبْغِ﴾. Most commonly in pause [it is] "نَبْغِ", following the codex (muṣḥaf), and after "نَبْغِ" there is a verse-end. It is also permissible — and it is better in Arabic — [to say] "ذَلِكَ ما كُنّا نَبْغِي" in pause. As for continuous speech, the better form in it is "نَبْغِي" with the yāʾ retained; this is the position of Abū ʿAmr, and it is stronger in Arabic. The meaning of the saying of Moses — upon him be peace — "ذَلِكَ ما كُنّا نَبْغِ" is: "that is what we were seeking", because he had been promised al-Khaḍir at the place where the fish would slip away. ﴿فارْتَدّا عَلى آثارِهِما قَصَصًا﴾, that is: they went back along the way they had travelled, following the trail closely; "اَلْقَصَصُ" is following a trail.

zajjaj:65-65.t: ﴿فَوَجَدا عَبْدًا مِن عِبادِنا آتَيْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا وعَلَّمْناهُ مِن لَدُنّا عِلْمًا﴾: by this al-Khaḍir is meant. It was said that he was named "al-Khaḍir" (the green one) only because whenever he prayed in a place, what was around him turned green. In what Moses did — and he was among the greatest of the prophets and had been given the Torah — of seeking knowledge and journeying [for it], there is what indicates that no one should abandon seeking knowledge, even if he has reached its utmost and encompassed most of what the people of his time grasp, and that he should be humble towards whoever is more knowledgeable than he.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿قالَ لَهُ مُوسى هَلْ أتَّبِعُكَ عَلى أنْ تُعَلِّمَنِي مِمّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا﴾, and "رَشَدًا". [The patterns] "اَلْفُعْلُ" and "اَلفَعَلُ", as in "اَلرُّشْدُ" and "اَلرَّشَدُ", are common in Arabic, as in "اَلْبُخْلُ" and "اَلْبَخَلُ" (miserliness), "اَلْعُجْمُ" and "اَلْعَجَمُ" (non-Arabs), and "اَلْعُرْبُ" and "اَلْعَرَبُ" (Arabs).

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿قالَ إنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾: this is al-Khaḍir's saying to Moses. Then he told him the reason for his not being patient, saying: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلى ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْرًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 68], that is: and how can you be patient with what appears outwardly to be reprehensible? For the prophets and the righteous are not patient with what they see as reprehensible.

zajjaj:69-69.t: ﴿قالَ سَتَجِدُنِي إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ صابِرًا﴾: this is Moses's saying to al-Khaḍir.

zajjaj:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ فَإنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِي فَلا تَسْألْنِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ حَتّى أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنهُ ذِكْرًا﴾, that is: if you find it objectionable, do not hasten to ask until I explain to you the reason for it. The accusative of "خُبْرًا" [in the previous verse] is as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "لَمْ تَحِطْ بِهِ" is "you have not known it by experience (لَمْ تَخْبُرْهُ خُبْرًا)". Similar to it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
؎وَصِرْنا إلى الحُسْنى ورَقَّ حَدِيثُنا ورُضْتُ فَذَلَّتْ صَعْبَةٌ أيَّ إذْلالِ
(We came to fair terms, our talk grew tender, and I tamed [her], so a refractory one became utterly submissive.)
Because the meaning of "رُضْتُ" (I tamed) is "أذْلَلْتُ" (I made submissive); and likewise "أحَطْتُ بِهِ" is in the sense of "خَبُرْتُهُ" (I knew it by experience).

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا رَكِبا في السَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَها﴾, that is: al-Khaḍir holed it. ﴿قالَ أخَرَقْتَها لِتُغْرِقَ أهْلَها﴾, and [it is also read] "لِيَغْرَقَ أهْلُها". His holing of it was on the side next to the water, because the exegesis has come that he holed it by pulling out two planks on the side next to the water. So he said: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إمْرًا﴾; the meaning of "إمْرًا" is: something enormous among reprehensible things.

zajjaj:72-72.t:
﴿قالَ ألَمْ أقُلْ إنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾: then when Moses saw that the water did not enter through the hole and that it did not harm those in the ship, ﴿قالَ لا تُؤاخِذْنِي بِما نَسِيتُ ولا تُرْهِقْنِي مِن أمْرِي عُسْرًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 73]. The meaning of "تُرْهِقُنِي" is "تُغَشِّينِي" (overwhelm me), that is: treat me with ease, not with hardship.
His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا لَقِيا غُلامًا فَقَتَلَهُ﴾ [al-Kahf: 74] means: al-Khaḍir killed him. ﴿قالَ أقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 74]: they said about "زَكِيَّةً": innocent, that is, nothing was seen that would require its being killed. "نُكْرًا" is less than his saying "إمْرًا", because drowning those in the ship was, in his view, more reprehensible than killing a single soul. It has also been said that "نُكْرًا" here means: "you have done something more reprehensible than the first matter." "نُكْرًا" is accusative in two ways: one of them means "you have done a reprehensible thing", and it is possible that its meaning is "you have come with a reprehensible thing (جِئْتَ بِشَيْءٍ نُكْرٍ)"; when the bāʾ was dropped, the verb reached [the noun] directly and made it accusative.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
﴿قالَ إنْ سَألْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدَها﴾, that is: after this question. ﴿فَلا تُصاحِبْنِي﴾ is also read "فَلا تَصْحَبْنِي", and there is an anomalous (shādhdh) reading "فَلا تُصْحِبْنِي". Whoever reads "فَلا تَصْحَبْنِي", its meaning is: "then do not be my companion." Whoever reads "فَلا تُصاحِبْنِي", its meaning is: "if I seek your companionship, do not go along with me in that." Whoever reads "تُصْحِبْنِي" — there are four possibilities in it, the best of which is: "then do not go along with me in that"; one says "قَدْ أصْحَبَ المُهْرُ" (the colt has become tractable) when it submits to being led, so its meaning would be: "then do not comply with me in anything I ask of you." It is also possible that its meaning is "then do not give me anyone as a companion", but I know of no sense for this, because Moses had not asked al-Khaḍir to give him anyone as a companion. [Translator's note: the text announces four possibilities but sets out only two.]
His saying: ﴿قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَدُنِّي عُذْرًا﴾ is also read "مِن لَدُنِي" with the nūn single (unstressed), because the original form of "لَدُنْ" has a quiescent [nūn]; so when you attach it to yourself [the first person], you add a nūn so that the quiescence of the first nūn may be preserved. You say "مِن لَدُنْ زَيْدٍ", making the nūn quiescent, then you attach it to yourself and say "مِن لَدُنِّي", just as you say "عَنْ زَيْدٍ" and "عَنِّي". Whoever says "مِن لَدُنِي" may not say "عَنِي" and "مِنِي" with the nūn dropped, because "لَدُنْ" is a non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) noun, whereas "مِن" and "عَنْ" are two particles that came for a meaning; moreover "لَدُنْ" is heavier than "مِن" and "فِي". The evidence that dropping the nūn is permissible in nouns is their saying "قَدْنِي" in the sense of "حَسْبِي" (enough for me); they say "قَدْ زَيْدٍ" [i.e. enough for Zayd], and they insert the nūn, for the reason we mentioned, when it is attached [to the first-person pronoun]; and "قَدِي" with the nūn dropped is permissible, because "قَدْ" is a non-declinable noun. The poet said — using both forms:
؎قَدْنِيَ مِن نَصْرِ الخُبَيْبَيْنِ قَدِي
(Enough for me of helping the two Khubaybs — enough for me!)
As for their making the dāl of "لَدْنِ" quiescent, they made it quiescent just as they say "عَضْدٌ" for "عَضُدٌ", dropping the "ṣifa". [Translator's note: the text reads "الصِّفَة" here; the sense requires "the ḍamma" (الضَّمَّة), i.e. dropping the vowel, and "الصفة" is probably a copyist's error.]

zajjaj:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿فانْطَلَقا حَتّى إذا أتَيا أهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ اسْتَطْعَما أهْلَها فَأبَوْا أنْ يُضَيِّفُوهُما﴾ is also read "أنْ يُضِيفُوهُما". One says "ضِفْتُ الرَّجُلَ" (I stayed with the man as a guest), meaning: I lodged with him; and "أضَفْتُهُ" and "ضَيَّفْتُهُ" when I lodged him and offered him hospitality.
His saying: ﴿فَوَجَدا فِيها جِدارًا يُرِيدُ أنْ يَنْقَضَّ فَأقامَهُ﴾, that is: al-Khaḍir set it upright. As for the meaning of "a wall wanting (جِدارًا يُرِيدُ)": will is only found in a manifestly living being, and the wall does not will with a real will; but its appearance of being ready to fall had become evident, just as the actions of those who will and intend become evident, so it was described as willing, since the two appearances are the same. This is frequent in poetry and in the language. Al-Rāʿī said, describing camels:
؎فِي مَهْمَهٍ قَلِقَتْ بِهِ هاماتُها قَلَقَ الفُؤُوسِ إذا أرَدْنَ نُضُولا
(In a trackless desert where their heads shook like axe-heads when they "want" to fly off [their handles].)
And another said:
؎يُرِيدُ الرُّمْحُ صَدْرَ أبِي بَراءٍ ∗∗∗ ويَعْدِلُ عَنْ دِماءِ بَنِي عَقِيلِ
(The spear "wants" the breast of Abū Barāʾ, and turns away from the blood of Banū ʿAqīl.)
It is read "أنْ يَنْقَضَّ" and "أنْ يَنْقاضَّ". "يَنْقَضَّ" means: it falls quickly; and "يَنْقاضَّ" means: it splits lengthwise. One says: "اِنْقاضَّ سِنُّهُ" when his tooth has split lengthwise.
His saying: ﴿قالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا﴾ is also transmitted as "لَتَخِذْتَ". That is because when the two of them stopped at the town, its people did not host them nor give them lodging, so Moses said: "If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for setting up this wall." It is read "لَتَخِذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا"; one says "تَخِذَ يَتْخَذُ" for "اِتَّخَذَ يَتَّخِذُ". The origin of "تَخِذَ" is from "أخَذْتُ", and the origin of "اِتَّخَذْتُ" is "اِئْتَخَذْتُ".

zajjaj:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ هَذا فِراقُ بَيْنِي وبَيْنِكَ﴾: Sībawayh held that the sense of something like this is emphasis (tawkīd), and the meaning is "this is the parting of what is between us", that is: "this is the parting of our connection." He said: and similar to this in the way speech works is "أخْزى اللَّهُ الكاذِبُ مِنِّي ومِنكَ" (May Allah disgrace the liar of me and you). So the mention of "بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ" a second time is emphasis. This can only be with the wāw; "هَذا فِراقُ بَيْنِي فَبَيْنِكَ" is not permissible, because the meaning of the wāw is togetherness, while the meaning of the fāʾ is that the second comes after the first. [Translator's note: the example is printed with "الكاذِبُ" in the nominative; the expected form as object of "أخْزى" is "الكاذِبَ".]

zajjaj:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿أمّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكانَتْ لِمَساكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ في البَحْرِ﴾: "مَساكِينُ" is a diptote (does not take full declension), because it is a plural that does not have the pattern of a singular. Likewise every plural such as "مَساجِدُ", "مَفاتِيحُ" and "طَوامِيرُ" is a diptote, as we have mentioned; we have explained this earlier in the chapter on diptotes.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ وراءَهم مَلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا﴾: he used to seize by force every ship that had no defect, but if it was defective he would not interfere with it. "وَراءَهُمْ" means: behind them; this is the better of the two views. It is possible that their return on their way passed by him and they did not know about him, so Allah informed al-Khaḍir about him. It was also said that "كانَ وراءَهُمْ" means: he was in front of them; this occurs in Arabic, because whatever is before you and in front of you, once it is hidden from you, has become "behind you". The poet said:
؎ألَيْسَ ورائِي إنْ تَراخَتْ مَنِيَّتِي لُزُومُ العَصا تُثْنى عَلَيْها الأصابِعُ
(Is there not, "behind" me [i.e. ahead of me], if my death is delayed, clinging to a staff over which the fingers are bent?)

zajjaj:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأمّا الغُلامُ فَكانَ أبَواهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينا أنْ يُرْهِقَهُما طُغْيانًا وكُفْرًا﴾: "يُرْهِقَهُما" means: drive them to "رَهَق", which is ignorance [i.e. folly].
His saying "فَخَشِينا" is from the speech of al-Khaḍir. Some people said: "فَخَشِينا" cannot be from Allah, and they said: "Our evidence that 'فَخَشِينا' is from the speech of al-Khaḍir…" [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source; the evidence is not stated in this entry.]

zajjaj:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأرَدْنا أنْ يُبْدِلَهُما رَبُّهُما خَيْرًا﴾: it is permissible for "فَخَشِينا" to be from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because khashya (fear) on the part of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, means dislike, while on the part of human beings it means fear.
His saying ﴿فَأرَدْنا﴾ is in the sense of "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, willed", because the wording of reports about Allah in this manner is more than can be counted. The meaning of ﴿وَأقْرَبَ رُحْمًا﴾ is: closer in affection and more closely bound by kinship. "اَلرُّحْمُ" and "اَلرَّحْمُ" in the language mean affection and mercy. The poet said:
؎وَكَيْفَ بِظُلْمِ جارِيَةٍ ومِنها اللِّينُ والرُّحْمُ
(How [could one] wrong a young girl, from whom come gentleness and tenderness?)

zajjaj:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ تَحْتَهُ كَنْـزٌ لَهُما﴾: it was said that the treasure was knowledge, and it was said that the treasure was wealth. What is well known in the language is that "treasure" (الكَنْز), when used on its own, means buried and stored-up wealth; and when it is not wealth, one says: "He has knowledge, and he has a treasure of understanding." "اَلْكَنْزُ" here is more likely wealth, because knowledge can hardly be learned except through a teacher, whereas wealth does not need anyone else for one to benefit from it. It is possible that the treasure was wealth on which knowledge was written, because it is related that it was a tablet of gold on which was written: "لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ" (There is no god but Allah; Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah). This is wealth and also great knowledge: the affirmation of the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the announcement that Muḥammad would be sent.
His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾: "رَحْمَةً" is accusative in two ways. One of them is His saying: "So your Lord willed, and we willed what we mentioned, as a mercy", that is: for the sake of mercy — "we did that as a mercy" — as you say: "I saved you from destruction out of mercy for you." It is also possible that "رَحْمَةً" is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of ﴿فَأرادَ رَبُّكَ أنْ يَبْلُغا أشُدَّهُما ويَسْتَخْرِجا كَنْـزَهُما﴾ is "Allah had mercy on them by that". And all that was mentioned, from his saying ﴿فَأرَدْتُ أنْ أعِيبَها﴾ [al-Kahf: 79] and his saying ﴿فَأرَدْنا أنْ يُبْدِلَهُما رَبُّهُما﴾ [al-Kahf: 81], means: "Allah had mercy on them a mercy."
His saying: ﴿وَما فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أمْرِي﴾ indicates that he did it by revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَسْألُونَكَ عَنْ ذِي القَرْنَيْنِ﴾: the Jews had asked about the story of Dhū al-Qarnayn by way of a test. ﴿قُلْ سَأتْلُو عَلَيْكم مِنهُ ذِكْرًا﴾: it is said that he was called "Dhū al-Qarnayn" (the one with two horns) because he had two braids. It is related from ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — that he said: he was called "Dhū al-Qarnayn" because he was struck on the right side of his head and the left side of his head, that is, he was struck on the two "horns" (sides) of his head. It is also possible — according to the view of the lexicographers — that he was called "Dhū al-Qarnayn" because he reached the two extremities of the world, the rising place of the sun and its setting place.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ سَبَبًا﴾ ﴿فَأتْبَعَ سَبَبًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 85], also read "فاتَّبَعَ"; that is: "We gave him of everything, by which he could attain, in [his] firm establishment, the regions of the earth, a means (سَبَب)", that is: "knowledge that would bring him wherever he wished", just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, subjected the wind to Solomon. The meaning of "فَأتْبَعَ سَبَبًا" — and Allah knows best — is: he followed one of the means that he had been given.

zajjaj:86-86.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ الشَّمْسِ وجَدَها تَغْرُبُ في عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ﴾ is read "حَمِئَةٍ" with the hamza. [Translator's note: the text here repeats "حَمِئَةٍ" as the variant; the other reading discussed below is "حامِيَةٍ".] Whoever reads "حَمِئَةٍ" means "in a spring having black mud (حَمْأة)". One says "حَمَأْتُ البِئْرَ" when I removed its black mud, and "أحْمَأْتُها" when I threw black mud into it, and "حَمِئَتْ هِيَ تَحْمَأُ فَهي حَمِئَةٌ" when black mud has come to be in it. Whoever reads "حامِيَةٍ" without the hamza means "hot"; and it may be hot and also have black mud. ﴿وَوَجَدَ عِنْدَها قَوْمًا﴾, that is: at the spring.
His saying: ﴿قُلْنا يا ذا القَرْنَيْنِ إمّا أنْ تُعَذِّبَ وإمّا أنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted him these two rulings, just as He permitted Muḥammad ﷺ to judge between the People of the Book or to turn away from them.

zajjaj:87-87.t:
﴿قالَ أمّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إلى رَبِّهِ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذابًا نُكْرًا﴾, that is: we shall punish him by killing, and Allah's punishing him with the Fire is more terrible than the punishment of killing.
His saying: ﴿وَأمّا مَن آمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا فَلَهُ جَزاءً الحُسْنى﴾ [al-Kahf: 88] is also read "جَزاءُ الحُسْنى". The meaning is: "he will have the best as a reward"; "جَزاءً" is a maṣdar (verbal noun) placed in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: "he will have the best, being rewarded with it as a reward." Whoever reads "جَزاءُ الحُسْنى" makes "جَزاءُ" muḍāf (in a genitive construct) to "اَلْحُسْنى"; both have been read. ﴿وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِن أمْرِنا يُسْرًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 88], that is: we will speak to him with fine words.

zajjaj:89-89.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أتْبَعَ سَبَبًا﴾, that is: another means, of those that would bring him to one of the regions of the earth.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ الشَّمْسِ وجَدَها تَطْلُعُ عَلى قَوْمٍ لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهم مِن دُونِها سِتْرًا﴾, that is: We had not given them anything to shade them, neither a roof nor clothing.
His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ [al-Kahf: 91]: it is possible that [it means] he found it rising upon a people like that tribe who were at the setting place of the sun, and that their ruling was the ruling of those.

zajjaj:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أتْبَعَ سَبَبًا﴾, that is: a third means, of those that would bring him to one of the regions of the earth.

zajjaj:93-93.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ﴾ is also read "بَيْنَ السُّدَّيْنِ". It was said: whatever is blocked by nature is a "سُدٌّ", and whatever is the work of people is a "سَدٌّ".
His saying: ﴿وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِما قَوْمًا لا يَكادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلا﴾ is also read "يُفْقِهُونَ", and its meaning is: they could hardly make [others] understand.

zajjaj:94-94.t:
﴿قالُوا يا ذا القَرْنَيْنِ إنَّ يَأْجُوجَ ومَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ في الأرْضِ﴾: "يَأْجُوجَ ومَأْجُوجَ" is read with the hamza and also read without the hamza. They are two foreign (non-Arabic) nouns and are diptotes, because they are definite. Some lexicographers said: whoever pronounces the hamza seems to derive it from "أُجَّةُ الحَرِّ" and from His saying "مِلْحٌ أُجاجٌ" (salty and bitter); "أُجَّةُ الحَرِّ" is the intensity and blaze of heat, and from this comes their saying "أجَّجْتُ النّارَ" (I kindled the fire). The [morphological] pattern of "يَأْجُوجَ" would then be "يَفْعُولَ", and of "مَأْجُوجَ" "مَفْعُولَ". It is possible that omitting the hamza is on this same meaning; and it is possible that "ماجُوجَ" is "فاعُولَ", and likewise "ياجُوجَ". This would be their derivation if the two nouns were Arabic; but foreign words are not derived from Arabic.
His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا﴾ is also read "خَراجًا". As for whoever reads "خَرْجًا": "اَلْخَرْجُ" is fayʾ (revenue), and "اَلْخَراجُ" is a levy (ḍarība); it was also said: the jizya (poll tax). According to the grammarians, "اَلْخَراجُ" is the noun for what is paid out of the obligations upon properties, and "اَلْخَرْجُ" is the maṣdar.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَلى أنْ تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَهم سَدًّا﴾, that is: "that you make between us and Gog and Magog."

zajjaj:95-95.t:
﴿قالَ ما مَكَّنِّي فِيهِ رَبِّي خَيْرٌ﴾; "ما مَكَّنَنِي" with two nūns is also permissible. That is: "What my Lord has established me in is better for me than the tribute you would give me." Whoever reads "مَكَّنِّي" assimilates the nūn into the nūn because the two nūns come together; whoever reads "مَكَّنَنِي" with two nūns pronounces both nūns distinctly, because they belong to two words: the first is from the verb, and the second comes in with the attached pronoun.
His saying: ﴿فَأعِينُونِي بِقُوَّةٍ﴾, that is: with work you do with me, not with money. ﴿أجْعَلْ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهم رَدْمًا﴾: "اَلرَّدْمُ" in the language is more than a barrier (السَّدّ), because "اَلرَّدْمُ" is what is laid one part upon another; one says "ثَوْبٌ مُرَدَّمٌ" (a patched garment) when it has been patched with one patch over another.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿آتُونِي زُبَرَ الحَدِيدِ﴾, that is: "pieces of iron". The singular of "اَلزُّبَرُ" is "زُبَرَةٌ", which is a large piece.
His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا ساوى بَيْنَ الصَّدَفَيْنِ﴾ is also read "اَلصُّدُفَيْنِ" and "اَلصُّدْفَيْنِ"; they are the two sides of the mountain.
His saying: ﴿قالَ انْفُخُوا﴾: that is, he took the great pieces of iron, put firewood and charcoal between them and set bellows to them, until they became like fire; this is His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا جَعَلَهُ نارًا﴾. When iron is heated with charcoal and bellows, it becomes like fire.
His saying: ﴿آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا﴾: the meaning is: "give me molten metal (قِطْر)", which is copper. So he poured the melted copper over the iron, which had become like oil, and it mixed and stuck together until it became a solid mountain of iron and copper. It is said that it is in the region of Armenia.

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَما اسْطاعُوا أنْ يَظْهَرُوهُ وما اسْتَطاعُوا لَهُ نَقْبًا﴾, that is: they were unable to climb over it because of its height and smoothness, and they were unable to bore through it.
His saying: ﴿فَما اسْطاعُوا﴾, without the tāʾ, is originally "اِسْتَطاعُوا" with the tāʾ; but the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ share one point of articulation, so the tāʾ was dropped because they came together, and so that the pronunciation would be lighter. Some Arabs say "فَما اسْتاعُوا" without the ṭāʾ, but reading with it is not permissible. And some of them say "فَما أسْطاعُوا" with the disjunctive alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), the meaning being "فَما أطاعُوا", the sīn being added. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: they added it as compensation for the loss of the vowel of the wāw, because the origin of "أطاعَ" is "أطْوَعَ". As for whoever reads "فَما اسْطّاعُوا" [Translator's note: printed here as "اسْطاعُوا", but the context shows the reading with the sīn assimilated into the ṭāʾ, i.e. with a doubled ṭāʾ, is meant], assimilating the sīn into the ṭāʾ, he commits a solecism and is in error; so held the grammarians al-Khalīl, Yūnus, Sībawayh and all who follow their view. Their argument for that is that the sīn is quiescent, and when the tāʾ is assimilated it becomes a quiescent ṭāʾ, and two quiescent letters cannot be combined. And whoever says: "I throw the vowel of the tāʾ onto the sīn and say 'فَما اسَطاعُوا'" is also in error, because the sīn of "اِسْتَفْعَلَ" is never given a vowel.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Kahf (The Cave)
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أنْـزَلَ عَلى عَبْدِهِ الكِتابَ ولَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجًا﴾ ﴿قَيِّمًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 2]: the exegetes and the lexicographers said that its meaning is: "Praise be to Allah, who sent down upon His servant the Book, upright (qayyiman), and did not put any crookedness in it". The meaning of "qayyim" is straight. "Al-ʿiwaj", with kasra on the ʿayn, is used of what has no visible body, and of what has a body one says "ʿawaj", with fatḥa on the ʿayn; you say "there is ʿiwaj (crookedness) in his religion" and "there is ʿawaj in the stick", with fatḥa on the ʿayn. Its interpretation is: "Thanks be to Allah who sent down upon Muḥammad the Book, straight, and did not put any crookedness in it", i.e. He did not put any contradiction in it, as He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلافًا كَثِيرًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 82].

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِن لَدُنْهُ﴾, i.e. to warn them of the dire punishment; ﴿مِن لَدُنْهُ﴾: from Him. ﴿وَيُبَشِّرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصّالِحاتِ أنَّ لَهم أجْرًا حَسَنًا﴾: the meaning is "that they will have (bi-anna lahum) a good reward".

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿ماكِثِينَ فِيهِ أبَدًا﴾: "ماكِثِينَ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the meaning of "abiding forever (khālidīna)".

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن أفْواهِهِمْ﴾ — "كَلِمَةٌ" is also read; [i.e. it is read] with the nominative and the accusative. Whoever reads it in the accusative, the meaning is: "their saying 'Allah has taken a son' is grievous as a word", so "كَلِمَةً" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Whoever read "كَلِمَةٌ", in the nominative, the meaning is: "grievous is a word, namely their saying: Allah has taken a son". In "كَبُرَتْ" it is also permissible to say "كَبْرَتْ كَلِمَةً", with sukūn on the bāʾ, but I know of no one who read it so.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ عَلى آثارِهِمْ إنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أسَفًا﴾: its interpretation is "perhaps you will destroy yourself"; some said: "kill yourself", and the meaning is the same. The poet said:
؎ألا أيُّهَذا الباخِعُ الوَجْدُ نَفْسَهُ لِشَيْءٍ نَحَتْهُ عَنْ يَدَيْهِ المَقادِرُ
(O you whose own soul grief is destroying, for something the decrees of fate have taken from his hands!)
The meaning is: "O you whose soul grief has destroyed". The meaning of "عَلى آثارِهِمْ" is: after them. ﴿إنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أسَفًا﴾: by "the discourse" the Qurʾān is meant. "أسَفًا" is accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). "Al-asaf" is extreme grief or anger; one says "qad asifa al-rajul, fa-huwa asīf wa-āsif". The poet said:
؎أرى رَجُلًا مِنهم أسِيفًا كَأنَّما ∗∗∗ يَضُمُّ إلى كَشْحَيْهِ كَفًّا مُخَضَّبا
(I see a man among them grief-stricken, as though he were clasping to his flanks a hand dyed [with blood].)

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿لِنَبْلُوَهم أيُّهم أحْسَنُ عَمَلا﴾, i.e. to test them. "أيُّهُمْ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), except that its form is the form of the interrogative; the meaning is "that He may find out whether this one is better in deeds or that one". So the meaning is: "We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, i.e. a test and a trial; and the one who is good in deeds is the one who renounces what has been made attractive to him of this world".

zajjaj:8-8.t: Then He made known to them that He will annihilate and bring to nothing all of that, and said: ﴿وَإنّا لَجاعِلُونَ ما عَلَيْها صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا﴾. "Al-ṣaʿīd" is the road on which there is no vegetation, and "al-juruz" is the land that grows nothing, as though it devoured the vegetation completely. One says "arḍun juruz" (barren land) and "araḍūna ajrāz" (barren lands).

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتَ أنَّ أصْحابَ الكَهْفِ والرَّقِيمِ كانُوا مِن آياتِنا عَجَبًا﴾: as for "al-raqīm", it has been said that it is the name of the mountain in which the cave was; and "al-kahf" (the cave) is like a ravine, or like a cavern in the mountain.

It has also been said that "al-raqīm" is the name of the village in which they lived; and it has been said that "al-raqīm" is a tablet on which there was writing, in the place where they were — and Allah knows best. It has also been said: the idolaters had asked the Prophet ﷺ about the spirit, about the people of the cave and about Dhū al-Qarnayn. That was because the affair of the Prophet ﷺ in Mecca had exhausted them, so a group of them went to Yathrib and told a group of the leaders of the Jews the story of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Jews said: "His name is written with us, and [it is written] that he will be sent after an interval between the messengers; so ask him about these things: if he answers about them, he is a prophet." So the group of idolaters went back to Mecca, gathered a large gathering, and asked the Prophet ﷺ about these things. He told them that he did not know them, and that if revelation came down to him about them he would inform them.

Some narrated that he said: "I will tell you about them", and did not say "if Allah wills", so revelation was delayed from him for some days, and there was revealed: ﴿وَلا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إنِّي فاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 23] ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Kahf: 24]. Then the Prophet ﷺ told them what Allah had revealed to him and sent down in His Book, which indicated the truth of his prophethood.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the story of the people of the cave is not a wonder among the signs of Allah, because we witness in the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, of what indicates the Oneness of Allah, what is more wondrous than the story of the people of the cave. So He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتَ أنَّ أصْحابَ الكَهْفِ والرَّقِيمِ كانُوا مِن آياتِنا عَجَبًا﴾, i.e. [do not think so] until We make their story clear. [Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]

zajjaj:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ هَذا رَحْمَةٌ مِن رَبِّي﴾, that is: this power by which I accomplished the barrier is a mercy from my Lord. "فَإذا جاءَ وعْدُ رَبِّي جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا وكانَ وعْدُ رَبِّي حَقًّا" is also read "دَكّاءَ", on the pattern "فَعْلاءَ", O reader (يا هَذا). "اَلدَّكّاءُ" and "اَلذَّكاءُ" [Translator's note: so printed, with dhāl in the second word; probably a copying error for a form of "دكّاء"] mean any elevated part of the ground that has been levelled flat. It means that when the Day of Resurrection comes, or at the time of the emergence of Gog and Magog, this mountain will become levelled; and the evidence that this mountain will become levelled is His saying: ﴿وَحُمِلَتِ الأرْضُ والجِبالُ فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 14].

zajjaj:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا بَعْضَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ في بَعْضٍ﴾: the meaning of "they surge (يَمُوجُونَ) in a matter" is: they plunge into it and talk about it a great deal. It is possible that by "يَوْمَئِذٍ" the Day of Resurrection is meant, and the evidence for that would be: ﴿وَنُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَجَمَعْناهم جَمْعًا﴾. It is also possible that "وَتَرَكْنا بَعْضَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ في بَعْضٍ" means: on the day the matter of the barrier was completed.
His saying "يَمُوجُ": they surged about, marvelling at the barrier. As for the meaning of "نُفِخَ في الصُّورِ", the lexicographers said: "اَلصُّورُ" is the plural of "صُورَةٌ" (form); but what has come in exegesis is that the ṣūr is a horn into which Isrāfīl blows — and Allah knows best — unless you take it to mean that at that blowing the resurrection of the servants and their raising up take place.

zajjaj:100-100.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَعَرَضْنا جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَرْضًا﴾: the interpretation of "عَرَضْنا" is: We made Hell manifest to them until they witnessed it and saw it.

zajjaj:101-101.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ كانَتْ أعْيُنُهم في غِطاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed a covering over their sight because of their unbelief. ﴿وَكانُوا لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا﴾: because of their enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ, they were unable to listen to what was recited to them, just as you say to someone who hates what you say: "You cannot bear to hear my words."

zajjaj:102-102.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبادِي مِن دُونِي أوْلِياءَ﴾: its interpretation is: "Do they think that their taking My servants as protectors will benefit them?!" It was also read — and it is a good reading — "أفَحَسْبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا", its interpretation being: "Is it then enough for them to take [My] servants as protectors besides Allah?!" Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear their recompense, saying: ﴿إنّا أعْتَدْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ نُـزُلا﴾. One says of anything taken to be stayed in: "أعْتَدْتُ لِفُلانٍ كَذا وكَذا" (I prepared such-and-such for so-and-so), that is: I took it as a provision (عَتاد) for him. "نُزُلًا" is in the sense of "مَنزِلًا" (a lodging).

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِالأخْسَرِينَ أعْمالا﴾: ["أعْمالًا"] is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), because when He said "بِالأخْسَرِينَ" (the greatest losers), it indicated that they had something they lost, so He made clear in what kind that loss occurred. He, Majestic and Mighty, made known that no deed done along with disbelief in Him is of any benefit at all, and said: ﴿الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهم في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Kahf: 104], as He the Exalted said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1]. "اَلَّذِينَ" can be genitive or nominative: the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of "اَلْأخْسَرِينَ", and the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), the meaning being: "They are those whose effort is lost in the life of this world." ﴿وَهم يَحْسَبُونَ﴾ [al-Kahf: 104], also read "يَحْسِبُونَ", ﴿أنَّهم يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 104], that is: they think, by their turning [people] away from the Prophet ﷺ, that they are doing good work.

zajjaj:107-107.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كانَتْ لَهم جَنّاتُ الفِرْدَوْسِ نُـزُلا﴾: people differed on the explanation of "اَلْفِرْدَوْسِ". Some said: "اَلْفِرْدَوْسُ" are the valleys that grow various kinds of plants. And they said: "اَلْفِرْدَوْسُ" is the orchard. And they said: it is Greek (bi-l-rūmiyya), carried over into Arabic wording; and "اَلْفِرْدَوْسُ" is also likewise in Syriac — the word "فِرْدَوْسُ". We have not found it in the poetry of the Arabs except in a verse of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
؎وَإنَّ ثَوابَ اللَّهِ كُلَّ مُوَحِّدٍ جِنانٌ مِنَ الفِرْدَوْسِ فِيها يُخَلَّدُ
(The reward of Allah for every believer in His oneness is gardens of Paradise (al-firdaws), in which he will abide forever.)
Its true meaning is that it is the orchard that combines everything found in orchards, because it is so among the people of every language; for this reason Ḥassān ibn Thābit said "gardens of the firdaws", and their saying that it is the orchard confirms this. "اَلْجَنَّةُ" in the language is also the orchard, except that the Garden which the believers will enter contains what is found in orchards [and more]; and what indicates this is His saying: ﴿وَفِيها ما تَشْتَهِيهِ الأنْفُسُ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 71].

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لا يَبْغُونَ عَنْها حِوَلا﴾, that is: they will not want any removal from it. One says: "قَدْ حالَ في مَكانِهِ حِوَلًا" (he moved from his place), just as they said among the maṣdars (verbal nouns): "صَغُرَ صِغَرًا" (to be small), "عَظُمَ عِظَمًا" (to be great), and "عادَنِي حُبُّها عِوَدًا" (love of her returned to me). It has also been said that "اَلْحِوالُ" means stratagem (الحِيلَة); on this meaning it would be: "they will not contrive [to seek] a dwelling other than it."
